_why: The Executive Summary versions ITSELF. Until r1.002 the page took its label from the living document's release counter, so it read v.19 r1.006 — a number that moves whenever the DOCUMENT changes and tells a reader nothing about the text in front of them. The operator's correction: 'this version is the default for executive summary, if easier maybe this should be r1.002'. Append an edition when the text changes; never renumber one that has shipped.

editions.note: First edition — Executive Summary to Humanity. The 1 + 12 deep dive: Preamble, twelve sections and a close, in plain international English.

Final approved text. The three-term hierarchy is now stated rather than implied — Thought Mastery the discipline, a Thought Master the person, Master of Thought the responsibility behind both. Vision • 2525 throughout. Master of Thought is responsibility rather than rank; that distinction is fundamental. The seal caption no longer claims cuneiform is the oldest writing we still have. Source filenames are out of the visible prose.

Opening tightened so the reading starts at the Preamble. Operator: 'when executive summary is clicked I dont want to see all the vision 2525 explanation; it should go straight to preamble.' Measured at 390px: the first sentence moved from 417px to 313px, and the Preamble now lands on the first screen. Text unchanged — same source hash as r1.002. Between-section spacing untouched at 40px.

Visible version line removed from the page masthead — versioning lives on the main Vision • 2525 document, per the operator. The machine stamps remain as invisible provenance: exel-release and exel-source-sha256 in the head, so a reader can still prove which edition and which text they hold. Text unchanged — same source hash as r1.002/r1.003.

Language globe moved into the page flow — a slim row above the masthead, right-aligned. Operator: 'make sure EN globe is at top above the text and not free floating.' Fixed positioning had floated it over the eyebrow on phones; in flow it can never overlap a word. Text unchanged.

A way back. '← Vision • 2525' joins the top row, left of the globe — a relative sibling link, so served and downloaded copies both return to the living document. The wordmark stays verbatim in every language, because it is a name. Text unchanged.

Tracking rule adopted: one SHA = one edition. Backfilled map of editions to the commits that shipped them: r1.002=b13a67b · r1.003=a42d5f6 · r1.004=fd09a96 · r1.005=d8718d9 · r1.006=51b407a · r1.007=13519fc (translation batches 860021d, 3cc1eab, 93d95e3 landed under r1.006–r1.007). Text unchanged.
Romanian lands — the Romance set (fr es pt it ro) is complete. 25 of 32 languages verified. Text unchanged.
Hebrew and Korean land — 29 of 32 languages verified (r1.009's note undercounted at 25; the true tally then was 27 with el and sw arriving mid-commit). Remaining: ja vi th. Text unchanged.
Finnish lands — 30 of 32 verified. Correction to r1.010's note on the record: ja had already shipped at r1.008; the remainder then was fi vi th, not ja vi th. Remaining now: vi th. Text unchanged.

Headers match the living document. Operator: 'use the same format as vision - 2525 for headers.' The heading grammar is copied from Vision • 2525 rather than approximated — Iowan Old Style serif stack at weight 600 with -.012em tracking, wordmark h1 at clamp(38,8.4vw,66)/1.02 +.02em, section h2 at clamp(20,3.4vw,26)/1.24, eyebrows as 700 11px ui-monospace at .16em; Fraunces retired. Vietnamese also lands — 31 of 32 verified; remaining: th. Text unchanged.

The language dropdown matches the living document. Operator: 'same here for drop down; never recreate what was already executed.' The r276 lift took the globe's logic but redrew its panel; this finishes the lift — the living document's .regmenu/.langmenu grammar verbatim (8px/12px panel, 10.5px sans heading, 500 12.5px sans rows, inline 600 11px mono accent code, one-line LC • Native (English) rows, .42-opacity disabled rows), token names mapped to this page's palette. The Sumerian in-preparation note stays. Thai also lands — 32 of 32 languages verified; the translation program is complete. Text unchanged.

The controls carry the living document's deck grammar. Operator: 'notice globe standard for language and dropdown standard.' The globe becomes icon-only — no EN code label — with the deck's exact globe drawing (equator + meridian lens, 16px stroke-2) in the deck-button chrome: 1px rule border, 3px radius (9px in dark, as the document does it), 31px control height, accent while open. The download takes the deck's #bDL grammar: HI-violet border, 8px radius, hi-bg hover. Text unchanged.

Overreach reverted. Operator: 'Use the same globe icon and drop down format. I never said to change flcolor.' r1.014 had recoloured the DOWNLOAD to the deck's HI-violet — a change nobody asked for. The download is back to its approved r1.007 drawing: ink icon on a line-coloured circle, accent on hover. The globe icon and the dropdown keep the living document's format, exactly as named. Text unchanged.

Dark by default. Operator: 'go to dark, and only light if light is highlighted in Vision-2525 setting bar.' The summary now follows the living document's ground rather than the OS: it reads v2525.ground — the same localStorage key the document's Settings toggle writes — and stamps data-theme before first paint. Dark everywhere, including a downloaded file:// copy where storage is unreadable; light only when the reader chose light in the document's Settings. Text unchanged.

Cyan in the text. Operator, with the dark page live: 'for text for some cyan for executive summary.' The page's accent becomes the living document's AI cyan exactly — #00DAE6 on the dark ground, #0D6E86 on light — replacing the muted teal, so the eyebrows (EXECUTIVE SUMMARY TO HUMANITY, PREAMBLE, 01–12), the litany banner, the seal plate edge, and the control accents now read in the same cyan the document itself speaks in. Text unchanged.

The violet download, now asked. Operator, with both pages side by side: 'match download violet and style to Vision 2525.' The download takes the living document's #bDL grammar exactly — HI-violet border and glyph (#7A2C8C light / #D18BE0 dark), 8px radius, hi-bg on hover, the deck's 31px control height and 16px stroke-2 drawing. (r1.014 had done this unasked and r1.015 reverted it; this time it is the operator's instruction, on the record.) Text unchanged.

𒅴𒂠 The Sumerian edition ships — a SCHOLARLY DRAFT, and the operator's 'final attempt to show cuneiform Sumerian' done as meaning, never English spelled in signs (the prior attempt's failure, diagnosed in SUM_METHOD). 70 body+spine keys / 485 sentence records: transliteration is the Sumerian master, cuneiform derives from a Unicode-name-verified 155-reading sign table, locked 2025 names honored (EN SAG.KI), three-term hierarchy carried. The page reuses the shared chrome; a translit toggle shows a selected sentence's transliteration + literal gloss left, English master phrase right; DRAFT banner routes corrections to GitHub issues. Spiral-tested by the 48-fleet's first waves — findings fixed before ship: -ak genitive spellings, k70 punctuation, .pn card host, scroll drift, responsive sizing, correction channel, method drift. The globe's 𒅴𒂠 row goes LIVE as SUM · draft on all 34 pages. English master unchanged.

Fleet wave-2 consolidation on the Sumerian draft. Terminology locked one-verb-one-string across the two parallel step-lists (Observe = igi he2-bar · Imagine = igi sza3-ga he2-gar · Simulate = igi-bar he2-gar — the k40/k52 collisions Aset's voter caught); Spiritual Intelligence unified to gesztu2 zi-ka; the one bare dub he2-gi4 restored to the reduplicated coinage; three load-bearing coinages added to the METHOD glossary (Collective Intelligence, Spiritual Intelligence, imagination) and HI joined the verbatim list. The litany's study card now inserts after the seal plate, never inside the ul (invalid HTML, Enki). New standing gate exec-summary-verify-sum.mjs (Enlil/Odin/Krishna convergence) re-runs token lint + e-concat-vs-current-master + stamp/twin parity over all 70 keys on demand — the stale-after-refreeze silent failure is closed. Langmenu generator synced to the shipped SUM row (Krishna's time-bomb). English master unchanged.

Fleet wave-3 hardening, led by Thor's two empirically proven injection holes: ⟦…⟧ passthrough content is now escaped on the plain path too (the k69/k70 alt/caption vector), and the study data embeds with < escaped so a crafted record can never end the script early — both mattered because the public correction channel is an edit path. Odin's stale-page case closed structurally: the page now carries an exel-sum-src stamp (hash of sum.json + signmap) that verify-sum recomputes, so a corrected transliteration with an unrebuilt page fails loudly; and the gate is ENFORCED — pre-commit now runs verify-sum. Study card left-aligns under centered hosts (Enki); k18's 'sit' verb reads tusz (the KU sign's sitting reading — Thoth's hapax audit); METHOD states the coinage flags live in its glossary and that the automated gates are structural, with meaning guarded by the invited review (Sofia). English master unchanged.

RTL menu anchoring (Sofia w2): the language menu's two text-align:left rules become text-align:start, so the open menu's rows follow the page direction on the Arabic and Hebrew editions instead of staying LTR-anchored. Two tokens; all 34 pages rebuilt. On the record as standing debt, not fixed here: the globe chrome (back link, tooltips, Language heading, draft note) is English on all 34 editions — the chrome-translation pass — and the back arrow is unmirrored on RTL. Text unchanged.

Sentence references (operator: 'section out work in smaller chunks page.paragraph.sentence number first'). Every study sentence now carries an addressable reference shown FIRST on its card — 00.01.01 = Preamble paragraph 1 sentence 1, 01–12 the sections (P.00 the head, P.01–03 the paragraphs), 13 the close (13.01.01–10 the litany, then banner, mottos, author, seal). The METHOD's correction instructions cite by reference. Also: the method's two last overclaims scoped per Sofia's voter — the draft does not mark per-word doubt and now says so; a wrong glyph is impossible only per reading, and the reading choice is named as exactly what review corrects. English master unchanged. Discovery while testing: r1.021's own code comment about escaping closing script tags CONTAINED a literal closing script tag — the HTML parser ended the script inside the comment, and the study toggle had been broken on the shipped page since r1.021 (structural gates cannot see runtime breakage; the interactive Playwright pass caught it). Comment defused, toggle verified working: 00.01.01 on the Preamble's first sentence, 13.01.01 on the litany, 0 page errors.

Operator, on the globe: 'Use SUM not SUX reduce all other text.' The code already ships SUM (r1.019); the note under the row is now one line — 'Scholarly draft — corrections invited; method on the page.' — reduced in the template AND its generator in the same edition, so the two cannot drift (Krishna's rule). Text unchanged.

Security: the sign table's VALUES are now validated. Thor's voter found the one input the r1.021 injection fixes didn't cover — signmap.json values are emitted into HTML raw, so a poisoned value (reachable via the correction PR the page invites) shipped live img/onerror nodes and both gates passed it. The builder now fails closed unless every sign value is pure cuneiform (U+12000–U+1254F); all 156 real entries pass. And the pre-commit gate is made real: chmod +x on the hook, core.hooksPath set to .githooks (Thor: the hook was committed non-executable with no hooksPath, so it never fired). English master unchanged.

Sign legibility (Pangu's voter, evidence-backed): signs within one hyphenated word were concatenated with zero gap and adjacent wedges fused into one denser-looking sign. A narrow no-break space (U+202F) now sits between in-word signs — a stable ~2.8px seam at 390px against the ~6px word gap, with zero line-breaks inside a sign run. The load-bearing catch: cune()'s final /\s+/ collapse silently ate U+202F (JS \s includes it), so the seam is preserved only by collapsing ASCII whitespace alone — both edits land together or the fix no-ops. Honest limit kept: this is a seam, not a per-sign label; ruby remains the real answer when cune() is next restructured. English master unchanged.

Reading above every sign, by default (operator: 'default like divinity guide with sumerian pronunciation above each character of cuneiform'). Each cuneiform sign now carries its transliteration reading as a ruby <rt> annotation directly above it — the pinyin-over-hanzi pattern the Divinity Guide uses — always visible, no tap required. Line-height opened to 2.9 to seat the annotations; readings in accent mono. The study card (tap) still gives the full-sentence transliteration, literal gloss, English, and the page.paragraph.sentence reference. The plain path (alt text, caption) keeps reading-free glyphs. This is the ruby restructure Pangu's cell named as the real answer to sign fusion. English master unchanged.

Clarity + hardening after r1.027's ruby. Since the reading now rides above every sign by default, the control labeled 'translit' was misleading (transliteration is always visible) — relabeled 'study', its job now stated plainly: tap a sentence for its literal gloss, English, and page.paragraph.sentence reference. The draft banner says the reading sits above every sign. The inline study-data embed is hardened further — U+2028/U+2029 escaped alongside the existing < → u003c — closing the one remaining way a record could ever break the script in a stricter parser. (The operator's 'random text below the logo' screenshot was a stale cached build from the r1.021–r1.022 window, before r1.023 fixed exactly that leak; the shipped bytes since are balanced 3/3 scripts, headless-verified no leak, toggle works.) English master unchanged.

The cuneiform now renders everywhere. Operator: 'cuneiform needs updates.' The highest-impact update: the signs no longer depend on a Google font that tofus offline and on devices without a system cuneiform face. A 25.2KB subset of Noto Sans Cuneiform — exactly the 118 signs this edition uses — is inlined as a data-URI @font-face (Pangu's measured recommendation; +~11% page weight). SIL OFL 1.1 honored (docs/i18n/sum/font/OFL-NOTICE.md); regenerator scripts/exec-summary-sum-font.py re-subsets to the current signmap; verify-sum fails closed unless the page carries the current subset AND it covers every signmap codepoint, so a new reading can never tofu silently. The download twin is now fully self-contained. English master unchanged.

Transliteration above every visible phrase. Operator: 'is there transliteration mode throughout? It works for title; some phrases dont work.' The one visible phrase still lacking readings was the seal caption (k69, the author line under the eagle) — it was plain. It now renders ruby like everything else, but WITHOUT the tappable study wrapper, because it sits inside the author link where a study-card tap would fight the navigation. k00 (browser-tab title) and k70 (seal image alt) stay plain — neither can carry ruby. Every visible cuneiform phrase on the page now carries its reading above each sign. English master unchanged.

The human annotation loop. Operator: 'add Feedback on button to open up to each sentence so we can correct over time in Transliteration mode; input goes to Supabase for later recall and correction (like a human label / annotation system).' In study mode each sentence's card now carries a 'Suggest a correction' button that opens an inline form prefilled with the current transliteration, plus a note/source field. Sending POSTs to a new Supabase-backed Cloudflare Pages Function (functions/api/sum-feedback.js) keyed to the sentence's page.paragraph.sentence reference — a curator recalls every suggestion for one chunk and applies it to exec-summary.sum.json. Server-side keys only (SUPABASE_URL + SERVICE_ROLE), KV fallback so nothing is ever lost, and a prefilled GitHub-issue fallback on a downloaded offline copy. Table: backend/app/migrations/020_sum_feedback.sql. English master unchanged.

_tracking: ONE SHA = ONE EDITION (operator rule, 2026-08-28). Every commit that changes the Executive Summary — text, chrome, or translations — increments r1.### here in the same commit, and the commit subject carries the label, so git history IS the version ledger. Editions are appended, never renumbered.
